items.title: DeepAgents
items.claim: DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph, providing planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls.

items.title: DeepAgents
items.claim: For RefractRouter v0.1, DeepAgents serves as the fixed-DAG execution harness, but its autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation should remain disabled.

items.title: LangGraph
items.claim: LangGraph is a graph state machine framework supporting explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing, and is used by RefractRouter as the lower-level execution substrate for a fixed task DAG.

items.title: Pydantic AI
items.claim: Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs, useful when strict schemas are required, but is not a core dependency for RefractRouter v0.1 unless structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck.

items.title: DeepSeek Harness
items.claim: DSH (DeepSeek Harness) is an agent harness in which the agent loop itself is a plugin, and for RefractRouter v0.1 it is reserved for the outer validation environment rather than the core routing loop.

items.title: LLM routing research gap
items.claim: Existing LLM routing work mostly selects one model for an entire request, whereas RefractRouter investigates per-node model selection within a task DAG to improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier.

items.title: Task decomposition boundary
items.claim: Static task decomposition is an application-layer concern; the router takes the DAG as input and focuses on per-node model selection, with dynamic re-splitting deferred until node-level routing is validated.

items.title: Benchmark design
items.claim: A useful routing benchmark requires fixed task DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency, and the first benchmark should stay small enough to reproduce.

items.title: Scoring rubric
items.claim: The v0.1 scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure and readability, and HTML validity, and scoring prompts and rubric versions must be versioned with run records.
